GROWTH DURING TRANSITION
A DISCUSSION OF ISSUES FACING STATES

Damian W Betebenner
National Center for the Improvement of Educational Assessment
San Diego, CA June 22nd, 2015

STATES: MORE ALIKE THAN NOT

• Idaho, Michigan, and West Virginia

• All states were using student growth (SGPs) prior to assessment
transition.
• All states have the desire to use growth during the assessment
transition.
• All states envision dif culties communicating the results and use in
accountability within the landscape of changing assessments

CALCULATION & USE OF GROWTH

• Technical (calculation) issues versus accountability use/communication
issues.
• Barring the existence of signi cant oor/ceiling effects, calculation of
valid SGPs won’t be an issue.
• States that have already transitioned (e.g., Utah, Wyoming, and WIDA)
are able to calculate SGPs.
• Accountability use/communication more dif cult.

• Some states already battling bad impressions about student growth.

• “How can you calculate growth across different tests?”

THREE BROAD OPTIONS

1. Modify accountability and growth (start fresh) going forward.
2. Modify accountability system during transition and continue with same
SGP growth
3. Continue with same SGP growth and accountability system as before.

GROWTH: DISPELLING SOME MYTHS

• It isn’t as hard to understand as popular perception suggests!
• Calculation may be complicated, but knowing how to calculate
student growth is not synonymous with understanding student
growth:
• The number π is difficult to calculate but is simple to
understand conceptually.
• Height and weight percentiles associated with children are
difficult to calculate but are simple to understand
conceptually.
• Computational details are important, but often obscure a
simple conceptual basis.

GROWTH: DISPELLING SOME MYTHS
MYTH: VERTICAL SCALES SOLVE YOUR PROBLEMS

• States transitioning to SBAC will have access to a vertical/
developmental scale.
• Vertical/developmental scales allow users to compare (and
subtract) scaled scores from grade to grade.
• A vertical scale (i.e., gain scores) is not a “growth model”

GROWTH: DISPELLING SOME MYTHS
MYTH: VERTICAL SCALES SOLVE YOUR PROBLEMS

• Growth as an amount of change:
• What could be more simple?
• Like height or weight just calculate the amount of change.
• Requires a vertical scale (which Indiana has up to this year
and will have going forward) or a set of ordered performance
levels.
• Growth = Score Time 2 - Score Time 1
• Not as simple as it seems: Comparisons between students
often lead to wrong conclusions.

GROWTH: DISPELLING SOME MYTHS
MYTH: VERTICAL SCALES SOLVE YOUR PROBLEMS

Let’s step outside of education for an example:

GROWTH: DISPELLING SOME MYTHS
MYTH: VERTICAL SCALES SOLVE YOUR PROBLEMS

• Which high jumper improved more?
• Judy’s best changed 2 inches.
• Anna’s best changed 6 inches.
• An inch is an inch!!!
• But is an inch really
an inch???
• Change versus improvement.
• 2 inches for an elite
jumper is far more remarkable than 6 inches for a novice.

GROWTH: NEXT STEPS

• An assessment transition is an extreme version of what has happened annually
• Correlations are likely sufficient to make SGPs informative.
• Growth to standard possible using test linkage, but un-tested at this point.
• Calculation is not the biggest issue! Explaining results is the biggest issue.
• Good artists borrow, great artists steal:
• Numerous states have produced great materials to help communicate results.
